nodes.name: Giant sequoia
nodes.desc: Grows in a few Yosemite groves, including Mariposa. Fire heat opens its cones and clears seedbeds, and decades of fire suppression have limited regeneration.

nodes.name: California black oak
nodes.desc: A mid-elevation oak whose acorns were a staple for Indigenous peoples and feed deer, bears and woodpeckers.

nodes.name: Whitebark pine
nodes.desc: A high-elevation pine whose seeds feed Clark's nutcrackers. It is declining from blister rust, pine beetles and fire suppression.

nodes.name: Fireweed
nodes.desc: Fireweed and other green meadow plants feed deer, marmots and pikas. Meadows are the grazing ground herbivores and their predators gather around.

nodes.name: Mule deer
nodes.desc: Browses shrubs and trees and eats forbs and acorns. A main prey of cougars and sometimes bears and coyotes.

nodes.name: Yellow-bellied marmot
nodes.desc: Eats grasses, leaves and flowers in summer, then hibernates for about eight months. Whistles an alarm when coyotes or eagles appear.

nodes.name: American pika
nodes.desc: Stores plants as haypiles under talus. Killed by heat above roughly 25 C, so an early warning species for climate change.

nodes.name: Douglas squirrel
nodes.desc: Active all year and gnaws sequoia cone scales, knocking seeds loose. Also a prey item for bobcats.

nodes.name: Clark's nutcracker
nodes.desc: Feeds mainly on pine seeds and buries surplus caches, making it the main disperser of whitebark pine.

nodes.name: Acorn woodpecker
nodes.desc: Stores acorns in tree holes and eats insects. Recorded often around the oak woodlands.

nodes.name: American black bear
nodes.desc: Mostly plants such as berries, shoots and acorns, plus insects, carrion and deer fawns. Park managers use bear-proof food storage.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: A generalist hunter of rodents, marmots and sometimes deer, also feeding on carrion.

nodes.name: Bobcat
nodes.desc: Hunts squirrels, rodents, birds and occasionally deer fawns in the lower forests.

nodes.name: Red-tailed hawk
nodes.desc: Hunts ground squirrels, marmots and other small mammals and birds from the air.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: An opportunistic bird that scavenges carrion and scraps and takes eggs and small animals.

nodes.name: Cougar
nodes.desc: The park top predator, favouring large prey and mainly mule deer. Bears sometimes visit its kills.

nodes.name: Snowpack & snowmelt
nodes.desc: Winter snow melts through spring and feeds the Merced and Tuolumne rivers and meadows. Snowpack is shrinking and melting earlier.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Drives growth through the short dry summer. Most precipitation falls in winter.

nodes.name: Fire
nodes.desc: Lightning and past Indigenous burning cleared brush. Sequoias need fire to release seeds and clear seedbeds.

nodes.name: Granite-derived soil
nodes.desc: Thin soils over granite hold nutrients that plants and meadows draw on.

nodes.name: Fungi & soil decomposers
nodes.desc: Break down fallen needles, wood, carcasses and droppings and return nutrients to the soil.
